title: Test shared-provider Strands behavior with MLFLOW_USE_DEFAULT_TRACER_PROVIDER=false
answers: how to test strands autolog with a shared tracer provider
how to write a test for foreign OpenTelemetry spans in mlflow strands
simulate remote parent span in mlflow tracing test
body:
In tests/strands/test_strands_tracing.py, set MLFLOW_USE_DEFAULT_TRACER_PROVIDER to "false" via monkeypatch.setenv before calling mlflow.strands.autolog(), so MLflow attaches to a shared provider rather than its default one.
To create a foreign span, build an otel_trace.SpanContext with is_remote=True and a SAMPLED TraceFlags, wrap it in NonRecordingSpan and set_span_in_context, then start a span from otel_trace.get_tracer("external") with that context.
Assert the outcome with get_traces() being empty, which shows the foreign span was ignored rather than registered.
applies: Tests for Strands autologging that exercise shared OpenTelemetry provider behavior.
says: Strands autologging should ignore foreign spans when connected to a shared tracing provider.
External tracing spans are showing up unexpectedly in recorded Strands execution traces.
Verify that shared telemetry providers skip remote external spans during Strands tracing.
Traces should remain empty when external non-recording spans run under shared tracer providers.
Prevent third-party telemetry spans from polluting recorded Strands trace sessions.
search: In tests/strands/test_strands_tracing.py:test_strands_autolog_shared_provider_skips_foreign_span, test Strands autologging with a shared OpenTelemetry provider by setting MLFLOW_USE_DEFAULT_TRACER_PROVIDER to false. Simulate a foreign span using otel_trace.SpanContext with is_remote=True and SAMPLED TraceFlags wrapped in NonRecordingSpan, then start a span from external tracer context. Assert that get_traces() returns empty to verify that external foreign spans are ignored rather than registered by mlflow.strands.autolog().
